item.title: All Blacks and Springboks suffer second Nations Championship defeats
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/11/2026 The All Blacks and South Africa suffered their second defeats in the Nations Championship this morning, leaving South Africa in first place and New Zealand second in the Southern Hemisphere standings.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/11/2026

The All Blacks and South Africa suffered their second defeats in the Nations Championship this morning, leaving South Africa in first place and New Zealand second in the Southern Hemisphere standings.

The All Blacks lost to England 37-12, while the Springboks were edged out by Ireland 20-17.

Last week, four of the five Southern Hemisphere teams lost their matches, with Argentina the only exception.

Argentina are currently third on the points table and will take on France at 8.10 this morning.

Also at 8.10 this morning, the Wallabies will face Wales.

item.title: Arsenal extend Premier League lead after 2-all draw with Newcastle
item.description: Arsenal have moved six points clear at the top of the English Premier League following a 2-all draw against Newcastle United this morning. Arsenal took the lead through Eberechi Eze, who finished with a first-time shot.
item.content:encoded:
Arsenal have moved six points clear at the top of the English Premier League following a 2-all draw against Newcastle United this morning.

Arsenal took the lead through Eberechi Eze, who finished with a first-time shot.

However, a mistake by Martin Odegaard allowed Harvey Barnes to equalise for Newcastle before Malick Thiaw put the home side ahead.

Arsenal responded through Noni Madueke, who scored with the team's first shot of the second half to secure a point.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya was also forced off the field with a shoulder injury.

In other matches, Manchester City and Fulham played out a 1-1 draw, Bournemouth defeated Nottingham Forest 2-0, Leeds United thrashed Chelsea 4-1 while Aston Villa and Sunderland played out a nil-all draw.

Arsenal is leading 28 points followed by Brighton with 22 points, Manchester City is third with 22 points while Bournemouth is fourth with 18 points.

Fijian Latui’s indiscipline and repeated yellow cards proved costly in their 61–12 defeat to Ireland A
item.description: Fijian Latui’s indiscipline and repeated yellow cards proved costly in their 61–12 defeat to Ireland A this morning . Fiji made a promising start and even took the lead early in the first half, but their lack of discipline quickly changed the course of the match.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian Latui’s indiscipline and repeated yellow cards proved costly in their 61–12 defeat to Ireland A this morning .

Fiji made a promising start and even took the lead early in the first half, but their lack of discipline quickly changed the course of the match.

Three yellow cards within five minutes left Latui down to 12 players, and Mesake Doge’s second yellow card, resulting in a 20-minute red card, further damaged their chances.

Playing with a numerical advantage, Ireland capitalised on Fiji’s defensive weaknesses, using their forwards and attacking opportunities to run in nine tries.

Gus McCarthy and Daniel Ryan both scored twice as Ireland took full control of the contest.

Fiji's problems were not simply about their defence, but also their inability to maintain discipline under pressure.

Repeated infringements, a high tackle, deliberate knock-ons and scrum penalties allowed Ireland to dominate possession and territory.

Ultimately, Fiji Latui paid a heavy price for their ill-discipline.

Their attacking ability was evident in moments, but the number of cards and loss of players made it extremely difficult to compete against an Ireland XV side that took full advantage.

item.title: Fiji goes down 6-0 to Morocco in U17 World Cup opener
item.description: Fiji has suffered a 6-0 defeat to Morocco in its opening Group H match of the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar this morning. Morocco dominated the match, scoring three goals in the first half and adding another three in t he second half to secure a convincing victory.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji has suffered a 6-0 defeat to Morocco in its opening Group H match of the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar this morning.

Morocco dominated the match, scoring three goals in the first half and adding another three in t he second half to secure a convincing victory.

Following the defeat, Fiji will now turn their attention to their next match against Spain at 12.30am next Tuesday.

Fiji will then face China PR at 3am on Friday, in its final group-stage match.

This tournament will provide valuable learning opportunities and exposure for the team.

The FIFA U-17 World Cup final is scheduled for December 14th.

item.title: Police and Army share Ratu Sukuna Bowl after tense 8-8 draw
item.description: Police have retained the Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl for the fifth consecutive year after holding Army to an 8-8 draw in an intense contest, with Army failing to convert a penalty in the dying moments of the match. The two teams will now share the Bowl, with Police, as the current trophy holders, retaining it for the first six months before Army takes over for the next six months.
item.content:encoded:
Police have retained the Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl for the fifth consecutive year after holding Army to an 8-8 draw in an intense contest, with Army failing to convert a penalty in the dying moments of the match.

The two teams will now share the Bowl, with Police, as the current trophy holders, retaining it for the first six months before Army takes over for the next six months.

The Police team received its first red card in the 18th minute, with Sakiusa Vosayaco sent off following a dangerous tackle.

Army kicked off the Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl match, controlling the tempo in the first quarter and scoring a try in the 20th minute to lead 5-0.

Army dominated most of the first half but could not convert much of its territorial advantage into points.

Police made basic errors, which proved costly in the first half, with both teams attempting to play a territorial game.

It was a tense first half, with both sides struggling to find their rhythm.

Army began the second half with disciplinary issues, as their prop was shown a yellow card in the 42nd minute.

Police slowly found their rhythm in the second half and maintained possession during the opening quarter.

They scored their first try in the 50th minute when skipper James Brown won the line-out and led the charge, rumbling all the way to the try line to level the scores at 5-5.

Police were awarded another penalty and opted to kick for goal in the 54th minute, taking an 8-5 lead.

Army levelled the scores at 8-8 after being awarded a penalty in the 63rd minute.

It was an electric finish as Police tried their best to find a winning score, but Army's gutsy defence held firm.

Army were awarded a penalty in the 82nd minute and opted to kick for goal, but failed to convert, allowing Police to retain the Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl for the sixth consecutive year.

item.title: New faces named in Fijian 7s and Fijiana squads for Dubai and Cape Town
item.description: Several new faces will feature in the Fiji Airways Men's and Fijiana National 7s teams for the opening two legs of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town. The men's team will feature debutants Vilimone Raiqiso, Aquino Savenaca, Sanaila Daliga and Saimone Qeleca.
item.content:encoded:
Several new faces will feature in the Fiji Airways Men's and Fijiana National 7s teams for the opening two legs of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town.

The men's team will feature debutants Vilimone Raiqiso, Aquino Savenaca, Sanaila Daliga and Saimone Qeleca.

Tira Wilagi has been named captain of the side, with Akuila Dranivotua, Joseva Talacolo, Kavekini Tanivanuakula, George Bose and Aquino Savenaca also included in the starting line-up.

The reserves are Douglas Daveta, Iowane Teba, Ratu Filipe Sauturaga, Sanaila Daliga, Vuiviwa Naduvalo and Saimone Qeleca.

Meanwhile, the Fijiana 7s team will feature debutants Merewarita Neivosa, Kelerayani Luvu and Regan Chapman.

Ana Naimasi has been named captain of the Fijiana side, with Sesenieli Donu, Adi Salote Nailolo, Laisani Moceisawana, Reapi Ulunisau, Varanisese Qoro and Kelerayani Luvu named in the starting line-up.

The reserves are Mariana Talatoka, Regan Chapman, Atelaite Ralivanawana, Ivi Savu and Mere Vocevoce.

The Fiji Men's 7s team will face defending champions New Zealand in their opening pool match next Saturday at 8.36pm, before taking on France at 11.17pm.

They will face Spain in their final pool match on Sunday at 4am.

Meanwhile, the Fijiana 7s team will face Canada in their opening pool match next Saturday at 6.44pm, followed by Japan at 9.44pm.

They will take on New Zealand in their final pool match on Sunday at 2.52am.
